statement: The decomposability obstruction holds even when every squared real polynomial p_j is an arbitrary polynomial of total degree at most two in the real and imaginary coordinates of A and B. Specifically, if f_W(A,B)-gamma||B||_F^2 = sum_j p_j(A,B)^2 + sum_(h=1)^4 g_h(A) b^*H_h b is an exact polynomial identity, with A in C^(p x 2), B in C^(q x 2), the four real g_h the entries of A^*A-I_2, and H_h constant Hermitian, then W-gamma I=P+Q^Gamma for some PSD P,Q. For gamma>=0 this restricted SOS form cannot certify a witness negative on any PPT state, including the actual rational KG candidate paired with its explicit PPT source.
proof_degree_reduction: Set B=0 in the identity. Its left side and all multiplier terms vanish, so every real p_j(A,0) is identically zero. Hence each degree-at-most-two p_j consists only of a real B-linear term L_j(B), a real A/B-bilinear term D_j(A,B), and a real homogeneous B-quadratic term T_j(B). Set A=0 and B=t B_0 and compare the t^4 coefficient: sum_j T_j(B_0)^2=0 for every B_0, so each T_j vanishes. Thus p_j=L_j+D_j. Average the identity over independent fourth-root-of-unity global phases of A and B. The L_j*D_j terms average to zero. The averaged sum of L_j^2 is b^* S b for a constant Hermitian S>=0; the averaged sum of D_j^2 is represented as P+Q^Gamma_(b) with PSD P,Q, as established in the predecessor by resolving the four phase characters. Matching the terms independent of A now gives H_1+H_2=gamma I+S, and matching the A^2 B^2 coefficients gives M_W=P+Q^Gamma_(b)+sum_h G_h tensor H_h.
proof_conclusion: The Alice-auxiliary |1>, Bob-auxiliary |0> slice has zero M_W and gives 0=P_10+Q_10^Gamma_q+I_p tensor (H_2)_00. P_10 and Q_10 are PSD, so product-vector expectations imply -(H_2)_00>=0. The both-auxiliary-|0> slice gives W=P_00+Q_00^Gamma_q+I_p tensor (H_1)_00. Using H_1+H_2=gamma I+S, we obtain W-gamma I=[P_00+I_p tensor (S_00-(H_2)_00)]+Q_00^Gamma_q, with both bracketed matrices PSD. Thus W-gamma I is decomposable. The proof uses no sampled data or external theorem beyond elementary polynomial coefficient comparison, phase averaging and PSD compression.
limits: Only the specified Stiefel equalities with B-Hermitian quadratic multipliers, a constant gamma*||B||^2, and SOS squares of total degree <=2 are addressed; arbitrary other equality multipliers, norm-ball terms, higher-degree squares, or other certificate formats are not ruled out. This is not a proper-family or target impossibility theorem and does not decide the unreviewed candidate's 2-block positivity.
